subject: Onboarding: Throughput & Latency test schedule — NimbusHealth
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Andrew Lee <andrew.lee@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Onboarding: Throughput & Latency test schedule — NimbusHealth

Hi Andrew,

Thanks again for the time today. Per our call, attaching a proposed test plan and a short mutual action plan so we can get your onboarding benchmarked next week. High-level asks from our side:

- Test window: Wed Nov 4, 10:00–12:00 PT (2h). If that doesn't work, propose an alternative.
- Targets to validate: p95 latency <= 250ms for 64–256 token prompts; sustained throughput >= 180 qps; burst capacity to 400 qps for short windows.
- Failure modes to watch: p99 spikes, KV cache warmup effects, and sequence-length regressions at 512–1024 tokens.

Attached: nimbus-load-plan.xlsx (test matrix & k6 schedule). Monica will run the harness from a VM in us-west1 and share raw metrics; Laura will coordinate access and post-test action items.

Next steps: please confirm the window and share the service-account we should use for the test runner (or a short-lived API key). Also confirm whether you want us to run on hosted capacity or through your Dedicated pool for this run.

Thanks — looking forward to validating throughput and latency so we can finalize the SLA gates.

—Karthik

Andrew — thanks, confirmed. A few implementation details so the run is reproducible:

- Harness: k6 v0.40 + custom JS loader (attached: k6-script-v1.js). We'll run from a single runner in us-west1 with 8 vCPUs; pattern will be: 30s ramp, 90s steady, 30s spike repeated across 6 scenarios (varying prompt sizes).
- Endpoints: staging-infer-01.redwood.internal/v1/generate
- Auth: please provide the short-lived API key to monica.patel@redwood.com; we will redact in logs.
- Metrics capture: Prometheus + Grafana snapshot + raw CSV exports.

Attached: nimbus-load-plan.xlsx, k6-script-v1.js. We will run the first pass with hosted (no dedicated reservation) to demonstrate baseline cost/latency. If you want us to flip to Dedicated mid-run, we can, but would prefer to start hosted for an apples-to-apples comparison.

Monica

Date: 2026-11-04T15:46:00-07:00
Subject: Test results: Nov 4 run (raw CSV + graphs attached)

Team — run completed. Attaching the raw CSV and a condensed graph set. Quick summary:

- Baseline (hosted, 8 vCPU runner): sustained 185 qps average across mixed prompt sizes; peak bursts to ~410 qps for 45s windows.
- Latency: p95 = 220ms for 64–256 tokens; p99 spikes to ~480ms during cold KV-cache windows.
- Sequence-length impact: at 1024 tokens we saw p95 increase to ~1.1s; memory pressure caused slower tail latency.
- Errors: <0.1% 5xx, transient retryable during one spike window (likely VM I/O).

Actionable items we recommend:
1) Enable prefix/KV warm cache before production rollout (we can configure warmup hooks).
2) Consider Dedicated pool for consistently hitting sustained 250+ qps with tighter p99 budgets.
3) If long sequences are common, recommend quantization profile Q4_16 + model sharding (we can run a quick comparison).

Attachments: 20261104-nimbus-results.csv, latency-graphs.png

Happy to walk through the CSV; propose a 30-min follow-up tomorrow to walk the graphs with your SREs.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

—Andrew
